novelty.justification: The claim predicts that language-specific information is "strong in early layers," "suppressed in middle layers," and "re-emerging in late layers," with maximal cross-lingual intervention success at the middle trough; its novelty route is therefore a proposed layerwise phenomenon plus a quantitative decodability/causal relationship. Searches using “multilingual transformer early middle late language-specific representations,” “U-shaped language identity decodability layers,” “language-agnostic middle layers activation patching,” and “latent language multilingual LLM” point to Wendler et al., Do Llamas Work in English? (2024), as well as Lost in Multilinguality (2025), DALI-based middle-layer activation patching (2025), and Understanding Multilingualism in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs (2026), which collectively already describe early/late language-specific processing, language-agnostic middle computation, and privileged middle-layer cross-lingual intervention. Casting those established observations as a named U-shaped probe curve and correlating trough depth with transfer is a natural operational extension rather than a new core relationship, although that exact quantitative summary may not previously have been reported.
